static_traits.name: Wang Xinyi
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents and a younger sibling
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationship with parents due to Academic pressure; has friends and family support, but academic worries not easily expressed to others
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no history of psychological counseling or treatment in the past; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to identify and describe Anxiety and needs, fairly cooperative; neutral tone

basic_info.main_problem: Since a recent poor math test score, continuously worrying about being unable to graduate from High school, feeling overwhelmed and Anxious.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to better understand math content and improve grades, while significantly reducing persistent Anxiety; willing to communicate with the math teacher and explore seeking tutoring support.
growth_experiences: In middle school once thought English might fail, but through systematic review and practice with a tutor, finally earned a B — an experience that seeking help and effort can improve academics; but subjectively feels the current situation is different.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on academic grades and meeting others' (parents') expectations
If I fail in key exams, it means I am not competent enough/not smart enough

special_situations.event: Received unsatisfactory math test score last week
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one important exam goes badly, it means I will fail afterwards too, eventually unable to graduate and disappointing parents
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Studying doubly hard, asking classmates for help to compensate, but still repeatedly Anxious inside and avoiding deep discussion with parents
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may never graduate; I will disappoint my parents.

special_situations.event: When studying math alone or preparing for the next exam
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not learn it this time, the next exam will surely be worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly practices questions, studies for long hours but with low efficiency, hesitates whether to seek help from a teacher / tutor
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely fail the exam again next time.

special_situations.event: When discussing grades and graduation requirements with parents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not met their expectations, they will think I am no good
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces communication with parents about academic details, bearing pressure alone to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will surely be disappointed, thinking I am not good enough.

special_situations.event: When reviewing the overall academic situation and thinking of mathematics as a key subject required for graduation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one course goes poorly, the whole equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses only on failure evidence, ignoring other subjects or past positive experiences
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just no good overall; this poor test shows I will keep failing.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized through academics by parents and significant others, to be accepted and seen as a capable person
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointment, negation from not meeting academic standards, thus experiencing shame and rejection
defense_goal: Maintains self-esteem and a sense of control through high self-demands and withholding help-seeking
Avoiding exposing 'incompetence', to reduce the risk of being judged

object_relations.self_representation: A Student needing grades to prove value/a possible failure
object_relations.object_representation: Critics with high expectations who may be disappointed (parents)

object_relations.self_representation: A Student who seems incompetent once seeking help
object_relations.object_representation: Authority figures with judging and deciding power (Teacher)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others suggest seeking help from a teacher / tutor
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating seeking help with exposing incompetence, worrying about being looked down on or negated by authority
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use an Empathic and inquiring tone, first affirming the value placed on independence, then gently asking: besides 'harder material', what other concerns are there? Invite distinguishing facts from worries, using concretizing and Clarification open-ended questions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about parents' expectations and possible disappointment
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turns tension and fear into self-blame, believes all consequences are borne by oneself
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently reflecting the self-blame burden, inviting identification of emotions (Anxiety/shame) and boundaries; using a supportive, low-confrontation tone, encouraging first-person statements of feelings and distinguishing facts from evaluations.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to recall and integrate past positive experiences (such as improvement from middle-school tutoring)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to negate transferability with the 'this time is different' reason, reducing hope
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Replaying the 'this time is different' reasons with an accepting stance, inviting listing of similarities and differences; using gentle Socratic Questioning to help discover transferable resources.

manifestations: Knowing well that family and friends are supportive, yet finding it hard to express academic fears to them, tending to bear the pressure alone
Feels embarrassed and ashamed about seeking help, reducing in-depth communication with parents
The sense of pressure about graduation and academic choices/responsibilities increases, internalizing the consequences wholesale as personal responsibility
Interpreting 'seeking help' as weakening autonomy and competence

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizing the 'seeking help = lacking ability' rule as a rigid standard
Evaluating one's academic performance with 'must/should' language, believing one poor test equals failure

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Worrying seeking help will expose incompetence, over-scrutinizing oneself and hesitating
Cautious when communicating with parents or teachers about academic problems, avoiding going in depth

exception_events.target_problem: When receiving unsatisfactory exam scores, usually catastrophically predicting continued failure, feeling strong Anxiety affecting sleep and Learning, and hesitating whether to seek external help.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In a middle-school episode of thinking English might fail, did not blindly sink into Anxiety, but studied systematically with a tutor, earning a B, with markedly improved sense of mastery and grades.
exception_events.reason: Different actions: proactively sought tutoring support and persisted in practice; different understanding: breaking the problem down, focusing on skill improvement; different support: tutor providing targeted feedback and encouragement.

positive_force: Successful experience of markedly improving academics through tutoring
Has potential support resources from friends and family
Willing to try communicating with teachers and exploring external help
Able to self-observe negative thoughts and Anxiety effects
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, predicting the future, black-and-white thinking and overgeneralization
Self-worth overly attached to academic grades and parents' expectations
Shame/incompetence associations with seeking help leading to avoidance
Sleep and appetite affected, further amplifying Anxiety and attention difficulties

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Anxiety (with insomnia and Decreased appetite) when Learning math or talking about grades/graduation
antecedent: Seeing or working on math homework/exam questions
Thinking about upcoming exams and graduation requirements
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases such as catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, stacked with fear of disappointing her parents, amplify the consequences of failure and equate value with grades
target_behavior.function: Escaping evaluation and failure feelings in the short term, avoiding shame and negation scenarios
target_behavior.consequence: Learning Decreased efficiency, academic Performance declining further, Relationship tension with parents, Anxiety maintained and intensified

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding seeking help (hesitating or unwilling to seek help from teachers/tutors)
antecedent: Associating 'seeking help = lacking ability' when thinking of asking teachers/tutors for help
Feeling shame and risk of being judged after poor grades
target_behavior.core_reason: The internalized rule 'seeking help means incompetence', avoiding exposing inadequacy to protect self-esteem
target_behavior.function: Maintaining self-esteem and sense of control, reducing shame and discomfort of being judged in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Difficult points not effectively resolved, negative cycle maintained, Anxiety persisting
